method.title: NIST/SEMATECH: exploratory outlier screening (modified z score)
method.interpretation: Own-history symmetric application screens, not probabilities, fraud findings, error determinations or race calls. Peer statistics are context only and never veto a border trigger.
method.madZeroPolicy: Advanced context retains absolute guards and null modifiedZ at MAD0; own-history triggers do not require peers.

flags.label: Two-party share swing toward Democrats of at least 10pp
flags.description: Provisional review: This county’s Democratic/Republican two-party share changed by at least 10 percentage points from its 2022 baseline, independently of state-peer changes. Other votes are not assigned to either party. These application screening thresholds are not probabilities, error findings or evidence of fraud. Reporting progress and candidate changes may explain differences.

flags.label: Unusual Democratic vote-count growth with ordinary opposing growth
flags.description: Provisional review: Democrat counts increased at least 25% and 100 votes, at least 25 percentage points above same-state peer growth, with modified z >3.5 (MAD-zero absolute guard). Opposing-party growth is within |z|≤2, or within 10pp of its peer median when MAD=0. Reporting progress, candidate changes and voting patterns may explain this exploratory result; it is not an error or fraud finding.

notFlaggedReasons: Positive growth does not pass both the 25pp peer-distance and modified-z criteria.
Opposing-party growth is outside its ordinary peer range.

flags.description: Provisional review: Candidate/write-in race votes per 100 residents changed by at least 10 percentage points. These application screening thresholds are not probabilities, error findings or evidence of fraud. Reporting progress and candidate changes may explain differences.

flags.description: Provisional review: Candidate/write-in race votes per 100 residents changed by at least 10 percentage points. This race-vote proxy uses all residents including children; it is neither actual ballots nor eligible-voter turnout. These application screening thresholds are not probabilities, error findings or evidence of fraud. Reporting progress and candidate changes may explain differences.
